tasks.title: D71 — the reconnect replay is one transaction over a union budget and retires every line it supersedes
tasks.description: Make replay_all what its docstring already claims. ibkr/pacing.py gains generic_wait_for_batch(count) -> float (0.0 when count <= 1, else max(0.0, (count - 1) * (1.0 / settings.MAX_REQ_PER_SEC) - (now - self._last_req_time)) under the lock) and generic_batch(count), a contextlib.contextmanager that re-checks the wait and raises PacingExceeded(wait) from inside __enter__ (so the body never runs), sets _batch_remaining = int(count), and in finally clears it and calls record_request_slot(); throttle() gains one branch before the clock read that decrements _batch_remaining and returns, and reset_for_tests clears the counter. ibkr/subscription_manager.py gains _cancel_hooks / set_cancel_hook and replay_all becomes three phases: one union pre-check (rt_n = the RT_BARS entries, generic_n = len(pending) - rt_n, one PacingExceeded(max(rt_wait, generic_wait)) before any mutation), then every pending entry's reissue() in registry order inside `with pacing_manager.generic_batch(generic_n):` with a full unwind on any raise, then rebind + retire the old id through the entry's own resolver + move the registry key. ui/main_window.py installs the two resolvers beside `self.sub_manager = SubscriptionManager()` (RT_BARS -> _unregister_req_id(old) + rt_manager.unsubscribe(old); OPTION_LEGS -> _option_req_ids.pop(old, None) + md_manager.cancel_mkt_data(old)) and makes _replay_subscriptions' deferral replaceable with an epoch (self._replay_serial, read via getattr) in front of the same single QTimer.singleShot(int(e.wait_seconds * 1000), ...). The generic gate is the 20 ms minimum-interval gate derived from MAX_REQ_PER_SEC = 50 and RT sends never touch it, so generic_n = len(pending) - rt_n is exact; S0_TICKS is declared but nothing in production registers under it, so it contributes nothing to the union and the arithmetic stays correct if a hook is ever added. subscribe's frozen signature, its four test doubles and the _Entry field set are untouched.
acceptance_criteria: Given a subscription registry holding entries of more than one type (one RT_BARS entry plus two OPTION_LEGS entries, each carrying reissue/rebind) and a pacing manager whose generic gate will refuse after the first send, When one replay pass runs, Then zero reissues are attempted and the registry is unchanged, exactly one retry is scheduled for the reported wait, and after that wait a single pass reissues every entry exactly once, in registration order.

Given the same fixtures and a replay that completes, When the pass returns, Then the number of live subscriptions equals the pre-replay number, every old reqId was retired exactly once through its own type's resolver, and no new reqId is registered twice; a second replay from the settled state reproduces the same live count, the same per-id retire counts and the same new-id set.

Given a replay whose reissue phase raises after at least one entry has been reissued, When the pass unwinds, Then every reqId issued during that phase is retired, each successful entry's routing is rebound to its old reqId, the registry is identical to its pre-pass state (no old line was cancelled), and the exception propagates to the caller.

Given a replay with both budgets open throughout, When the pass runs, Then it returns the same [(old_req_id, new_req_id)] pairs in the same order as the pre-change pass, performs exactly one rebind per entry, and the pre-existing replay suites stay green with no assertion re-baselined.

Given PacingManager and an open generic batch of n, When throttle() is called n times, Then all n calls return without sleeping; an (n+1)th call inside the batch falls through to the unchanged minimum-interval gate and raises PacingExceeded when the interval has not genuinely elapsed; a throttle() call after the batch has closed behaves exactly as before; and reset_for_tests() clears the reservation so it can never admit a later send.

tasks.title: D72 + D75 + D76 — a cap-parked wave is a healthy, resumable state and a readiness loop stays bounded
tasks.description: One lifecycle, three faces. ui/ticker_session.py gains _wave_parked and _settle_parked_wave() (disarm the watchdog and stop _wave_continue_timer when _wave_parked and not self._history_req_ids; return whether it settled); the cap branch of _issue_wave_chunks sets _wave_parked = True after the unchanged status message and calls the settle step (it normally does not settle — members are in flight), and on_historical_data_end / on_historical_error call it before their _wave_may_complete() checks, so the bound is released at end/error/162/strand/disconnect settle time and only when the last in-flight member ends. _wave_parked is cleared by queue_wave_plans, _cancel_history_requests and _finalize_history_wave. _issue_wave_chunks' single except (PacingExceeded, IBKRNotReady) splits: PacingExceeded keeps _schedule_wave_continuation(wait); IBKRNotReady sets _wave_deferral_reason = "IBKR not ready", arms the watchdog only if not self._history_wave_timer.isActive() (base bound, no wait), surfaces one status line per episode (_wave_not_ready_announced), and starts the continuation at the unchanged 1 s fallback without re-arming; same split in _retry_silent_chunk. _schedule_wave_continuation gains one keyword-only transport_not_ready: bool = False so the default path is byte-identical. ui/main_window.py: _on_session_history_wave_timeout returns without stranding when session._wave_parked and not session._history_req_ids (the guard lives in the timeout handler ONLY — _finalize_stranded_history_wave stays unchanged so a disconnect still strands and drops the parked queue), and passes "IBKR not ready" when the session's _wave_deferral_reason names the transport, else "Historical backfill timed out"; _load_chart_resolved's coalesce gate widens to (bool(_history_req_ids) or bool(_wave_plan_queue)) and same triple, and for a parked session the coalesce branch resets _wave_issued_this_load = 0, clears _wave_parked, re-arms the watchdog, calls _issue_wave_chunks() and refreshes the indicator while leaving the queue's identity intact (no list(...) copy, no clear, no re-plan); an in-flight coalesce keeps today's no-op; set_backfill_state gains one derived marker word `parked` from a _backfill_parked latch set by _refresh_backfill_indicator as session._wave_parked and not session._history_req_ids and cleared in clear_backfill_indicator — signature, keys and idle line unchanged. The bound formula, both window fractions, per_load_historical_cap() and the D54 expiry block are untouched.
acceptance_criteria: Given a wave whose every issued member has ended and which stopped issuing at the per-load cap, When the clock advances past twice the watchdog bound, Then no stranded finalise occurs, _wave_plan_queue is intact (same length, same objects), the D53 indicator reports the parked/queued state, no timeout shortfall is recorded, and the watchdog timer is not active.

Given a cap-yielded wave with an in-flight member that never answers and no queue progress, When the watchdog bound elapses, Then the wave is finalised exactly once with the stranded reason and the AC-D16.4 shortfall line, and the queue is dropped exactly as before the change.

Given a parked wave, When the identical chart is loaded again, Then the oldest queued plan is issued first and the indicator leaves the parked state, the watchdog is re-armed for the resumed work, and the total number of requests issued across both loads stays inside the budget the pacing manager allows.

Given a session with queued plans and no in-flight ids for the current triple, When the identical triple is loaded, Then no cancel occurs, the plan queue keeps its identity and contents, _pending_prefetch survives, and no duplicate or extra request is issued for the parked plans beyond the queued plans themselves.
Given a parked wave and a load of a different symbol, timeframe or mode, When the load path runs, Then the existing cancel path runs, the generation advances, and the old queue is cleared.

Given a client that reports not-ready indefinitely, When the bound's worth of time passes, Then the wave ends through a bounded path — one finalise with a surfaced reason that names the transport, or one surfaced message after a bounded retry budget — and the retry count is bounded by the bound rather than growing with elapsed time; the bound is armed once per episode, never re-armed on the fixed short tick.

Given not-ready for two seconds and then readiness, When the wave continues, Then it issues as soon as readiness lands with one continuation at a time, and the watchdog arm arguments are the base bound for the deferral the episode actually covers.

Given a parked wave and a disconnect, When the disconnect path settles the wave, Then the parked queue is dropped and the wave is finalised exactly once — the parked guard exists only in the watchdog timeout handler, so the disconnect strand path is unchanged.

Nothing else in either path changes: the cancel, the tag, the post-issue slot, the _retried_plans allowance and the continuation/arm behaviour stay as they are; persisted rows are untouched because save_bars is INSERT OR REPLACE on the mode-aware PK. Then scope the ledger: queue_wave_plans also resets self._backfill_failed_req_ids = set() (beside _retried_plans) and calls the new _prune_cancel_tags(); _cancelled_history_gen: dict[int, int] records _history_generation at each _cancelled_history_req_ids.add(...) site (the cancel path and the silence retry); _register_history_request's existing discard also pops the gen entry; _prune_cancel_tags() keeps ids whose tagged generation is >= _history_generation - 1 and runs at the start of queue_wave_plans. is_superseded stays a set-membership read. tasks.description: Add tests/test_p26_fence.py — one assertion per named artefact of AC-D76.3 plus the module constants the phase relies on — and record the phase's delta scope. The D41-D70 assertion is presence per id in a heading, never a literal ### D<n> prefix (the record is mixed, exactly as P25's fence records). Read every value off the live modules (ui.ticker_session's per_load_historical_cap and the two window fractions, _history_wave_watchdog_bound_ms() against pacing_manager._hist_window, ibkr.subscription_manager's four tags, the include_types set _replay_subscriptions passes, ibkr.market_data.TIMEFRAME_CONFIG's keys), never off prose and never as a copied literal. Record git diff --name-only 629be4a in the wave result against the phase allowlist; list gates G3 and G4 as owner-run and do not claim them. Publish no literal file/line counts and no phase commit hash, so a later phase cannot redden this fence.
